#
# Inputs (CENTRAL only, outside git): Glyphbound/SourceArt/Weapons/Pistol/
#   Export/SM_Pistol_{Body,Trigger,Magazine,EnergyBar}.fbx  (Tools/Blender/pistol_export_fbx.py)
#   Textures/T_Pistol_{BaseColor,ORM,Normal,EmissiveMask}.png (Tools/Blender/pistol_prepare_ue.py)
# Output: /Game/Glyphbound/Weapons/Pistol/ (meshes, textures, materials, instances). Parameters the game sets
# (keep in sync with AGBGun, Source/Glyphbound/Weapons/GBGun.cpp):
#   ElementColor   (vector) the glow colour: the enchant element, or the gun's own colour when not enchanted
#   ImbueRemaining (scalar) M_GunEnergy only: cells with ImbueU < ImbueRemaining light up (0 = bar dark, 1 = full)
# Every material slot of every mesh must get a material from SLOT_MATERIALS, or the script fails.

import os
import re
import unreal

MESH_DIR = "/Game/Glyphbound/Weapons/Pistol"
SOURCE_DIR = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(unreal.Paths.project_dir(), "SourceArt", "Weapons", "Pistol"))
MESHES = ["SM_Pistol_Body", "SM_Pistol_Trigger", "SM_Pistol_Magazine", "SM_Pistol_EnergyBar"]
TEXTURES = {
    # name: (compression, sRGB)
    "T_Pistol_BaseColor": (unreal.TextureCompressionSettings.TC_DEFAULT, True),
    "T_Pistol_ORM": (unreal.TextureCompressionSettings.TC_MASKS, False),
    "T_Pistol_Normal": (unreal.TextureCompressionSettings.TC_NORMALMAP, False),
    "T_Pistol_EmissiveMask": (unreal.TextureCompressionSettings.TC_MASKS, False),
}
GUN_GREEN = unreal.LinearColor(0.02, 1.0, 0.07, 1.0)

# Blender material -> (parent material, {param: value}). Values copied from the Principled BSDF of each material
# (Tools/Blender/pistol_list_materials.py). Glow = Blender emission strength (emission colour = element colour).
SOLID = "M_GunSolid"
SLOT_MATERIALS = {
    "tripo_material": ("M_PistolAtlas", {}),
    "Refinished_gunmetal_panels": (SOLID, {"BaseColor": (0.83, 0.85, 0.88), "Metallic": 0.55, "Roughness": 0.28}),
    "Refined_dark_receiver": (SOLID, {"BaseColor": (0.055, 0.061, 0.07), "Metallic": 0.78, "Roughness": 0.32}),
    "FPS_SightHousing_Black": (SOLID, {"BaseColor": (0.027, 0.031, 0.039), "Metallic": 0.7, "Roughness": 0.36}),
    "Optic_Frame_Machined_Black": (SOLID, {"BaseColor": (0.025, 0.03, 0.038), "Metallic": 0.7, "Roughness": 0.3}),
    "Optic_Tinted_Transparent": ("M_GunGlass", {}),
    "Optic_Reticle_Element": (SOLID, {"BaseColor": (0.01, 0.01, 0.01), "Metallic": 0.0, "Roughness": 0.5, "Glow": 2.0}),
    "Panel_Finish_Bezel": (SOLID, {"BaseColor": (0.008, 0.012, 0.016), "Metallic": 0.75, "Roughness": 0.28}),
    "Panel_Finish_Element": (SOLID, {"BaseColor": (0.014, 0.02, 0.02), "Metallic": 0.1, "Roughness": 0.23, "Glow": 0.04}),
    "Panel_Finish_Graphics": (SOLID, {"BaseColor": (0.008, 0.012, 0.012), "Metallic": 0.1, "Roughness": 0.3, "Glow": 1.0}),
    "Trial_Magazine_DarkMetal": (SOLID, {"BaseColor": (0.04, 0.046, 0.055), "Metallic": 0.75, "Roughness": 0.3}),
    "Trial_Magazine_Silver": (SOLID, {"BaseColor": (0.43, 0.46, 0.49), "Metallic": 0.8, "Roughness": 0.28}),
    "V4_dark_metal": (SOLID, {"BaseColor": (0.027, 0.03, 0.038), "Metallic": 0.8, "Roughness": 0.35}),
    "V4_satin_edge": (SOLID, {"BaseColor": (0.1, 0.105, 0.12), "Metallic": 0.8, "Roughness": 0.3}),
    "Refined_vent_recess": (SOLID, {"BaseColor": (0.008, 0.01, 0.014), "Metallic": 0.45, "Roughness": 0.42}),
    "Refined_satin_silver": (SOLID, {"BaseColor": (0.63, 0.66, 0.69), "Metallic": 0.8, "Roughness": 0.28}),
    "V4_element_emission": ("M_GunEnergy", {}),
}

MEL = unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary
EAL = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary


def log(message):
    unreal.log("import_pistol: " + message)


def fail(message):
    unreal.log_error("import_pistol: ERROR " + message)
    raise RuntimeError(message)


def key(name):
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", name.lower())


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- import

def run_import(filename, options=None):
    task = unreal.AssetImportTask()
    task.filename = filename
    task.destination_path = MESH_DIR
    task.automated = True
    task.replace_existing = True
    task.save = False
    if options is not None:
        task.options = options
    unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().import_asset_tasks([task])
    paths = list(task.imported_object_paths)
    if not paths:
        fail("nothing imported from %s" % filename)
    return paths


def import_textures():
    textures = {}
    for name, (compression, srgb) in TEXTURES.items():
        source = os.path.join(SOURCE_DIR, "Textures", name + ".png")
        if not os.path.isfile(source):
            fail("missing %s" % source)
        run_import(source)
        texture = unreal.load_asset(MESH_DIR + "/" + name)
        if not isinstance(texture, unreal.Texture2D):
            fail("%s did not import as a Texture2D" % name)
        texture.set_editor_property("compression_settings", compression)
        texture.set_editor_property("srgb", srgb)
        texture.set_editor_property("lod_group", unreal.TextureGroup.TEXTUREGROUP_WEAPON)
        textures[name] = texture
        log("texture %s %s srgb=%s" % (name, compression, srgb))
    return textures


def fbx_options():
    ui = unreal.FbxImportUI()
    ui.set_editor_property("import_mesh", True)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_as_skeletal", False)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_materials", False)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_textures", False)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_animations", False)
    ui.set_editor_property("mesh_type_to_import", unreal.FBXImportType.FBXIT_STATIC_MESH)
    data = ui.static_mesh_import_data
    data.set_editor_property("combine_meshes", True)
    data.set_editor_property("auto_generate_collision", False)
    data.set_editor_property("generate_lightmap_u_vs", False)
    data.set_editor_property("remove_degenerates", False)
    data.set_editor_property("convert_scene", True)
    data.set_editor_property("force_front_x_axis", False)
    data.set_editor_property("import_uniform_scale", 1.0)
    data.set_editor_property("normal_import_method", unreal.FBXNormalImportMethod.FBXNIM_IMPORT_NORMALS)
    return ui


def import_meshes():
    # The legacy FBX importer honours FbxImportUI; with Interchange on, these options would be translated.
    unreal.SystemLibrary.execute_console_command(None, "Interchange.FeatureFlags.Import.FBX false")
    meshes = {}
    for name in MESHES:
        source = os.path.join(SOURCE_DIR, "Export", name + ".fbx")
        if not os.path.isfile(source):
            fail("missing %s (run Tools/Blender/pistol_export_fbx.py)" % source)
        run_import(source, fbx_options())
        mesh = unreal.load_asset(MESH_DIR + "/" + name)
        if not isinstance(mesh, unreal.StaticMesh):
            fail("%s did not import as a StaticMesh" % name)
        meshes[name] = mesh
    return meshes


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- materials

def get_or_create_material(name):
    path = MESH_DIR + "/" + name
    if EAL.does_asset_exist(path):
        material = EAL.load_asset(path)
        if not isinstance(material, unreal.Material):
            fail("%s exists but is not a Material" % path)
        MEL.delete_all_material_expressions(material)
        return material
    material = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().create_asset(
        name, MESH_DIR, unreal.Material, unreal.MaterialFactoryNew())
    if material is None:
        fail("could not create %s" % path)
    return material


class Graph(object):
    def __init__(self, material):
        self.material = material

    def node(self, cls, x, y, **props):
        e = MEL.create_material_expression(self.material, cls, x, y)
        if e is None:
            fail("could not create %s" % cls.__name__)
        for k, v in props.items():
            e.set_editor_property(k, v)
        return e

    def connect(self, src, out, dst, inputs):
        if isinstance(inputs, str):
            inputs = [inputs]
        for i in inputs:
            if MEL.connect_material_expressions(src, out, dst, i):
                return
        fail("cannot connect %s.%r -> %s.%r (inputs %s)" % (
            src.get_class().get_name(), out, dst.get_class().get_name(), inputs,
            list(MEL.get_material_expression_input_names(dst))))

    def out(self, src, out, prop):
        if not MEL.connect_material_property(src, out, prop):
            fail("cannot connect %s.%r -> %s" % (src.get_class().get_name(), out, prop))

    def vector(self, name, x, y, value):
        return self.node(unreal.MaterialExpressionVectorParameter, x, y, parameter_name=name,
                         default_value=unreal.LinearColor(value[0], value[1], value[2], 1.0))

    def scalar(self, name, x, y, value):
        return self.node(unreal.MaterialExpressionScalarParameter, x, y, parameter_name=name, default_value=value)

    def mul(self, a, b, x, y):
        m = self.node(unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, x, y)
        self.connect(a, "", m, "A")
        self.connect(b, "", m, "B")
        return m

    def rgb(self, src, x, y):
        m = self.node(unreal.MaterialExpressionComponentMask, x, y, r=True, g=True, b=True, a=False)
        self.connect(src, "", m, ["", "Input"])
        return m


def finish(material, name):
    errors = MEL.recompile_material(material)
    if errors:
        for e in errors:
            unreal.log_error("import_pistol: ERROR compile: %s" % e)
        fail("%s has compile errors" % name)
    bad = MEL.get_material_error_expressions(material)
    if bad:
        fail("%s: %d expressions report errors" % (name, len(bad)))
    log("material %s" % name)


def opaque(material):
    material.set_editor_property("blend_mode", unreal.BlendMode.BLEND_OPAQUE)
    material.set_editor_property("shading_model", unreal.MaterialShadingModel.MSM_DEFAULT_LIT)
    material.set_editor_property("two_sided", False)


def element_glow(g, x, y, glow_default):
    """ElementColor * Glow -> the emissive of a part that glows in the element colour."""
    color = g.rgb(g.vector("ElementColor", x, y, (GUN_GREEN.r, GUN_GREEN.g, GUN_GREEN.b)), x + 200, y)
    return g.mul(color, g.scalar("Glow", x, y + 150, glow_default), x + 400, y + 50)


def build_solid():
    # Plain PBR values per slot (instances set them) + optional glow in the element colour.
    m = get_or_create_material(SOLID)
    opaque(m)
    g = Graph(m)
    g.out(g.rgb(g.vector("BaseColor", -800, -300, (0.05, 0.05, 0.06)), -600, -300), "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_BASE_COLOR)
    g.out(g.scalar("Metallic", -800, -150, 0.75), "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_METALLIC)
    g.out(g.scalar("Roughness", -800, -50, 0.3), "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_ROUGHNESS)
    g.out(element_glow(g, -1000, 100, 0.0), "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_EMISSIVE_COLOR)
    finish(m, SOLID)
    return m


def texture_sample(g, texture, sampler, x, y):
    return g.node(unreal.MaterialExpressionTextureSample, x, y, texture=texture, sampler_type=sampler)


def build_atlas(textures):
    # The cleaned Tripo atlas: albedo, ORM (R AO, G roughness, B metallic), DirectX normal, and the glow mask
    # (Blender: emission strength 0.65 where the mask is set, in the element colour).
    m = get_or_create_material("M_PistolAtlas")
    opaque(m)
    g = Graph(m)
    base = texture_sample(g, textures["T_Pistol_BaseColor"], unreal.MaterialSamplerType.SAMPLERTYPE_COLOR, -900, -500)
    orm = texture_sample(g, textures["T_Pistol_ORM"], unreal.MaterialSamplerType.SAMPLERTYPE_MASKS, -900, -200)
    nrm = texture_sample(g, textures["T_Pistol_Normal"], unreal.MaterialSamplerType.SAMPLERTYPE_NORMAL, -900, 100)
    mask = texture_sample(g, textures["T_Pistol_EmissiveMask"], unreal.MaterialSamplerType.SAMPLERTYPE_MASKS, -900, 400)
    g.out(base, "RGB", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_BASE_COLOR)
    g.out(orm, "R", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_AMBIENT_OCCLUSION)
    g.out(orm, "G", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_ROUGHNESS)
    g.out(orm, "B", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_METALLIC)
    g.out(nrm, "RGB", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_NORMAL)
    glow = element_glow(g, -900, 650, 0.65)
    emissive = g.node(unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, -300, 500)
    g.connect(mask, "R", emissive, "A")
    g.connect(glow, "", emissive, "B")
    g.out(emissive, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_EMISSIVE_COLOR)
    finish(m, "M_PistolAtlas")
    return m


def build_energy():
    # The energy bar: dark metal; cells glow (strength 7 in Blender) where ImbueU (UV channel 1) < ImbueRemaining.
    m = get_or_create_material("M_GunEnergy")
    opaque(m)
    g = Graph(m)
    g.out(g.node(unreal.MaterialExpressionConstant3Vector, -600, -400,
                 constant=unreal.LinearColor(0.027, 0.03, 0.038, 1.0)), "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_BASE_COLOR)
    g.out(g.node(unreal.MaterialExpressionConstant, -600, -300, r=0.75), "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_METALLIC)
    g.out(g.node(unreal.MaterialExpressionConstant, -600, -220, r=0.34), "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_ROUGHNESS)
    uv = g.node(unreal.MaterialExpressionTextureCoordinate, -1200, 0, coordinate_index=1)
    u = g.node(unreal.MaterialExpressionComponentMask, -1000, 0, r=True, g=False, b=False, a=False)
    g.connect(uv, "", u, ["", "Input"])
    remaining = g.scalar("ImbueRemaining", -1000, 120, 1.0)
    one = g.node(unreal.MaterialExpressionConstant, -1000, 240, r=1.0)
    zero = g.node(unreal.MaterialExpressionConstant, -1000, 320, r=0.0)
    lit = g.node(unreal.MaterialExpressionIf, -800, 100)
    g.connect(u, "", lit, "A")
    g.connect(remaining, "", lit, "B")
    g.connect(zero, "", lit, ["A > B", "AGreaterThanB"])
    g.connect(zero, "", lit, ["A == B", "AEqualsB"])
    g.connect(one, "", lit, ["A < B", "ALessThanB"])
    glow = element_glow(g, -1000, 450, 7.0)
    g.out(g.mul(lit, glow, -400, 200), "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_EMISSIVE_COLOR)
    finish(m, "M_GunEnergy")
    return m


def build_glass():
    # Sight pane: Blender mixes 13% of a dark glossy surface over full transparency.
    m = get_or_create_material("M_GunGlass")
    m.set_editor_property("blend_mode", unreal.BlendMode.BLEND_TRANSLUCENT)
    m.set_editor_property("shading_model", unreal.MaterialShadingModel.MSM_DEFAULT_LIT)
    m.set_editor_property("two_sided", True)
    g = Graph(m)
    g.out(g.node(unreal.MaterialExpressionConstant3Vector, -600, -300,
                 constant=unreal.LinearColor(0.1, 0.13, 0.13, 1.0)), "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_BASE_COLOR)
    g.out(g.node(unreal.MaterialExpressionConstant, -600, -200, r=0.1), "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_ROUGHNESS)
    g.out(g.scalar("Opacity", -600, -100, 0.15), "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_OPACITY)
    finish(m, "M_GunGlass")
    return m


def make_instance(name, parent, params):
    path = MESH_DIR + "/" + name
    if EAL.does_asset_exist(path):
        mi = EAL.load_asset(path)
    else:
        mi = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().create_asset(
            name, MESH_DIR, unreal.MaterialInstanceConstant, unreal.MaterialInstanceConstantFactoryNew())
    if mi is None:
        fail("could not create %s" % path)
    MEL.set_material_instance_parent(mi, parent)
    for p, v in params.items():
        if isinstance(v, tuple):
            MEL.set_material_instance_vector_parameter_value(mi, p, unreal.LinearColor(v[0], v[1], v[2], 1.0))
        else:
            MEL.set_material_instance_scalar_parameter_value(mi, p, v)
    MEL.update_material_instance(mi)
    return mi


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- assign and check

def assign(meshes, masters):
    instances = {}
    for blender_name, (parent_name, params) in SLOT_MATERIALS.items():
        if parent_name == SOLID:
            instances[key(blender_name)] = make_instance("MI_Pistol_" + blender_name, masters[SOLID], params)
        else:
            instances[key(blender_name)] = masters[parent_name]
    for name, mesh in meshes.items():
        slots = mesh.get_editor_property("static_materials")
        for index, slot in enumerate(slots):
            slot_key = key(str(slot.material_slot_name))
            match = next((m for k, m in instances.items() if slot_key.startswith(k)), None)
            if match is None:
                fail("%s slot %d '%s' has no material in SLOT_MATERIALS" % (name, index, slot.material_slot_name))
            mesh.set_material(index, match)
        box = mesh.get_bounding_box()
        log("mesh %s slots=%d uv_channels=%d tris=%d bounds min=(%.1f, %.1f, %.1f) max=(%.1f, %.1f, %.1f)" % (
            name, len(slots), mesh.get_num_uv_channels(0), mesh.get_num_triangles(0),
            box.min.x, box.min.y, box.min.z, box.max.x, box.max.y, box.max.z))
    if meshes["SM_Pistol_EnergyBar"].get_num_uv_channels(0) < 2:
        fail("SM_Pistol_EnergyBar lost its ImbueU UV channel")


def main():
    if not EAL.does_directory_exist(MESH_DIR):
        EAL.make_directory(MESH_DIR)
    textures = import_textures()
    meshes = import_meshes()
    masters = {SOLID: build_solid(), "M_PistolAtlas": build_atlas(textures), "M_GunEnergy": build_energy(),
               "M_GunGlass": build_glass()}
    assign(meshes, masters)
    if not EAL.save_directory(MESH_DIR, only_if_is_dirty=False, recursive=True):
        fail("could not save %s" % MESH_DIR)
    log("OK")


main()

# Task: weapon tree rework and three new weapon perks

Project: **Glyphbound** (Unreal Engine 5.9.0, C++), in `Glyphbound/`. Read `Design/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `Prompts/implementer_rules.md` first (you DO build and run things in this task; the rest of "Hard rules" applies). One build or run at a time. Do not open the Unreal Editor. Do not commit.

Owner's request (translated): "Add these perks and fix the weapon branch. Precision Recovery heals a fixed 3% of max health, but its internal cooldown goes down with the ranks: 6 / 5 / 4 s. Deadeye gives +0.25x damage per rank." GDD v0.24, section 5 and section 18 "Weapon tree (owner, v0.24)". Every number below goes in data, never in code.

## 1. The new layout (`Content/Data/Skills.json`, tree `Weapon`)
Three columns (0 left, 1 middle, 2 right). Keep the existing node ids; change only `Column`, `Row`, `Requires` and what is listed here.

| Node | Id | Col | Row | Requires | Cost | Max rank | Modifiers per rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Heavy Rounds | `Weapon_Damage` | 1 | 0 | - | 1 | 3 | unchanged |
| Quick Trigger | `Weapon_FireRate` | 0 | 1 | Weapon_Damage | 1 | 3 | unchanged |
| Rapid Reload (new) | `Weapon_ReloadSpeed` | 0 | 2 | Weapon_FireRate | 1 | 3 | `Weapon.All.ReloadTime` Multiply 0.9 (stacks to -30% at rank 3) |
| Steady Grip | `Weapon_Recoil` | 0 | 3 | Weapon_FireRate | 1 | 3 | `Weapon.All.RecoilPitch` Multiply 0.8 **and** `Weapon.All.RecoilYaw` Multiply 0.8 |
| Marksman | `Weapon_Headshot` | 2 | 1 | Weapon_Damage | 2 | 3 | unchanged |
| Precision Recovery (new) | `Weapon_PrecisionRecovery` | 2 | 2 | Weapon_Headshot | 1 | 3 | `PrecisionRecovery` Add 1 (a player stat = the rank, see 2) |
| Arcane Conduit (new) | `Weapon_EnchantBuildUp` | 2 | 3 | Weapon_Headshot | 1 | 3 | `Weapon.All.EnchantBuildUpMult` Multiply 1.1 (stacks to +30%) |
| Deadeye (new) | `Weapon_PistolHeadshot` | 0 | 4 | Weapon_Damage | 1 | 3 | `Weapon.Pistol.HeadshotMult` Add 0.25 |
| Point Blank | `Weapon_ShotgunClose` | 1 | 4 | Weapon_Damage | 1 | 3 | unchanged |
| Long Shot | `Weapon_RifleFar` | 2 | 4 | Weapon_Damage | 1 | 3 | unchanged |

Check how a `Multiply` op scales with the rank (the architecture says linear per rank: 0.9 at rank 3 = 0.7) and confirm it in your report.

Descriptions (English, player-facing, short, in the same style as the others):
- Rapid Reload: "10% faster reloads per rank."
- Steady Grip: "20% less recoil per rank." (unchanged text)
- Precision Recovery: "Defeating an enemy with a head or weak point hit restores 3% of your max health. Cooldown 6 / 5 / 4 s by rank." (Read the 3% and the cooldowns from the data when building the text only if the HUD already supports that; otherwise a fixed string is fine.)
- Arcane Conduit: "+10% elemental build-up from enchanted weapons per rank."
- Deadeye: "Pistol: +0.25x head / weak point damage per rank."
Make sure the skill-tree screen (`UI/GBHUD_Menus.cpp`) draws 5 rows and the connector lines for these `Requires` cleanly (the spell tree already uses row 4; check the weapon tree does too, in both UI styles). Take a look at the layout in the smoke screenshot of the skill screen and fix overlaps if there are any.

## 2. Precision Recovery (new code)
- Rule: when an enemy dies and its **killing blow** was a head / weak point hit (`FGBDamageInfo::bHeadshot` on the killing blow) whose `Instigator` is the player, and the player has `PrecisionRecovery` rank >= 1 and the internal cooldown is over, the player heals `PrecisionRecoveryHealFraction` x max health and the cooldown starts. Once per enemy death by construction (a shotgun's pellets kill once). Hitting a head without killing never heals.
- Find where enemies die (`AGBEnemyCharacter`, `OnDied`, the attribute component's `OnDeath` carries the killing blow) and pick the cleanest hook that gives you the killing blow and its instigator; tell me which in the report. Keep the logic in the player (or a small component on the player), not in the enemy.
- `Game.json` `Values` (new): `PrecisionRecoveryHealFraction` 0.03, `PrecisionRecoveryCooldownBase` 7, `PrecisionRecoveryCooldownPerRank` 1, `PrecisionRecoveryCooldownMin` 1. Cooldown = max(Min, Base - PerRank x rank) -> 6 / 5 / 4.
- Pure function, static and testable (place it next to similar combat helpers, e.g. `UGBCombatLibrary`): `static float ComputePrecisionRecoveryCooldown(int32 Rank, float Base, float PerRank, float MinCooldown);` (rank <= 0 returns 0 = perk off; callers check the rank first). And the decision `static bool ShouldPrecisionRecover(bool bKillingBlowWeakPoint, bool bInstigatorIsPlayer, int32 Rank, float TimeSinceLastHeal, float Cooldown);`.
- Test `Glyphbound.Combat.PrecisionRecovery`: cooldowns 6/5/4 for ranks 1/2/3, rank 0 never heals, a body-shot kill never heals, another instigator never heals, inside the cooldown no heal, exactly at / after the cooldown heals. Check the test name rule (no name may be a prefix of another, e.g. not `Combat.Precision` next to it).
- Show a short heal feedback the way other heals show (a green damage-number-style "+N" if the damage numbers support heals, or the existing HUD message), no new UI system.
- Use a world-time stamp for the cooldown (not a timer per kill). Reset is not needed on death or checkpoint.
- `PrecisionRecovery` is a player stat key (no `Spell.` / `Weapon.` prefix): check how other player stat modifiers from skills reach the player (`UGBStatsComponent`, e.g. how `MoveSpeed` or another non-prefixed key works) and do it the same way.

## 3. Arcane Conduit (enchant build-up)
- New weapon stat `EnchantBuildUpMult` (add to `Core/GBStatNames.h`, value 1 in the `Stats` of every gun in `Weapons.json` so the modifier key is valid for the load-time check; keep the stat list in `GBGun.h`'s comment current).
- In `AGBHeldItem::MakeDamageInfo` (`Weapons/GBHeldItem.cpp`, the enchant branch near `GetActiveEnchant`): when the hit's element comes **from the enchant**, multiply `Info.BuildUp` by `GetStat(EnchantBuildUpMult, 1)`. The elemental sword's own element (not an enchant) is not affected. Keep the weak-point build-up rule as it is.

## 4. Rapid Reload
`ReloadTime` already goes through `GetStat` with modifiers; verify that the reload progress bar on the HUD follows the shorter time.

## 5. Smoke script (`Core/GBDevCommands.cpp`)
- Give the player the skills through the skill tree component (the smoke run already adds points and unlocks nodes for other checks; follow that), then:
  - Precision Recovery rank 1: set the player's health to 50% of max, kill a fresh weak enemy (or the training dummy if it can die; otherwise spawn an orc the way the smoke run already does) with a `DealDamage` killing blow that has `bHeadshot = true` and the player as instigator; log `SMOKE precision recovery healed=%.1f` (health gained), which must equal 3% of max health (+-0.5), else `UE_LOG(LogGB, Error, ...)`. Then a second weak-point kill right away must heal 0 (cooldown): `SMOKE precision recovery cooldown healed=%.1f`, must be 0.
  - Rapid Reload rank 3: log `SMOKE rapid reload pistol=%.2f` with the pistol's `GetStat(ReloadTime)`, which must be 0.7 x its base (+-0.01).
  - Arcane Conduit rank 3 with an enchanted gun: log `SMOKE arcane conduit buildup=%.2f base=%.2f` from `MakeDamageInfo` before and after; must be 1.3x (+-0.01).
- Take a screenshot `12_weapon_tree` of the weapon tree screen with a few of the new nodes unlocked.
- Reset the skills afterwards so the later smoke steps start from the same state as before (the reset exists: `UGBSkillTreeComponent::ResetAll`).

## Verification (all must be true when you finish)
1. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1` -> `Result: Succeeded`.
2. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Build-Jam.ps1 -Target Glyphbound` -> `Result: Succeeded`.
3. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Test-Jam.ps1 -MinTests 36` passes (35 today + yours).
4. `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File Tools/Jam/Smoke-Jam.ps1` ends with `Smoke: done=True crashed=False LogGB errors=0 timedOut=False`, with `SMOKE path check passed`, the new SMOKE lines, and no `LogGB` warning (the load-time modifier key check must stay silent).
Never make an error or a failing test disappear by changing the expected numbers or deleting behavior: if a check fails, fix the code. All JSON files stay valid.

## Final report (plain text)
1. The four result lines verbatim, plus the new SMOKE lines.
2. What you changed, with file names; the death hook you used for Precision Recovery and why; how `Multiply` scales with rank.
3. Anything you could not do as described, and why.
4. What a person should check by playing.

| `SM_Pistol_Magazine` | the magazine | its own centre | (-11.4, -4.7, -17.3) .. (8.1, 4.7, 11.9) |

Materials are already assigned on the meshes. Two parameters are for the game to set, on dynamic material instances:
- `ElementColor` (vector): exists on most slots (atlas glow, panel graphics, reticle, energy bar). Setting it on a slot that lacks it is harmless.
- `ImbueRemaining` (scalar 0..1): only on the energy bar's material. Cells light up from the grip end towards the muzzle as it grows; 0 = bar dark, 1 = full bar.

## 1. Which guns use it (data)
- Add `FString ViewModel` to `FGBWeaponDefinition` (`Data/GBDataTypes.h`), loaded from `Weapons.json` like the other fields (empty = the placeholder shapes, as today). Set `"ViewModel": "Pistol"` on the `Pistol` entry only. Shotgun and Rifle keep their placeholder shapes for now.

## 2. Building it (`Weapons/GBGun.h/.cpp`)
- In `BuildViewModel`, when `Definition.ViewModel == "Pistol"`: create four `UStaticMeshComponent`s (no collision, no overlap events, no shadow casting, like `AddPart`), load the meshes by path (`/Game/Glyphbound/Weapons/Pistol/SM_Pistol_Body.SM_Pistol_Body` etc.) and set them up:
  - `Body` attached to `Root`, relative scale `PistolViewScale` = 0.3 (uniform), location (0, 0, 0).
  - `EnergyBar` attached to `Body`, at (0, 0, 0).
  - `Trigger` attached to `Body`, relative location (28.84, 0, 0) (cm in the body's unscaled frame; the body's scale applies through attachment).
  - `Magazine` attached to `Body`, relative location (0, 0, -29.31).
  - Keep `Root->SetRelativeRotation(FRotator(0, -6, 0))` as today.
  - Put the numbers (scale, the two offsets, the motion values below) as named `constexpr` values in an anonymous namespace at the top of `GBGun.cpp`, with a one-line comment each saying where they come from (`Glyphbound/SourceArt/Weapons/Pistol/Export/export_report.json`, made by `Tools/Blender/pistol_export_fbx.py`). They are art tuning, not game balance, so they stay out of the JSON.
- If any of the four meshes fails to load (other machines do not have `Content/`), log ONE warning (`LogGB`) and build the placeholder shapes instead, so the game still runs.
- For every material slot of the four components, create a `UMaterialInstanceDynamic` (`CreateDynamicMaterialInstance`) and keep them in an array so the gun can set parameters every frame cheaply.
- Keep the placeholder path working exactly as today for the other guns.

## 3. Moving parts (Tick, only while the pistol viewmodel exists)
- **Trigger pull:** on every shot (`PerformAttack` that fires), play a short pull: the trigger's relative rotation goes from 0 to `FRotator(-8, 0, 0)` (pitch -8: the bottom of the trigger moves back towards the grip) and back to 0, over `TriggerPullSeconds` = 0.12 s in total (linear in, linear out). A new shot restarts it.
- **Magazine during reload:** drive it from `GetReloadProgress()` (0..1) while reloading. Offset from its rest location, in the body's frame, `MagazineOutOffset` = (-12.15, 0, -24.11) cm (back and down along the grip). Progress 0 to 1/3: slide out from rest to the full offset; 1/3 to 2/3: stay out; 2/3 to 1: slide back in. Smoothstep each slide. When not reloading (including a cancelled reload), it sits at rest. This mirrors the Blender animation (frames 24-40 out, 40-56 held, 56-72 in).
- **Glow colour and energy bar** (GDD 6, weapon enchant): every tick, ask `GetActiveEnchant(Element, Effect)`.
  - Enchanted: `ElementColor` = `GBPlaceholder::ElementColor(element)` on every slot, and `ImbueRemaining` = `TimeRemaining / TotalDuration` of that enchant's status effect (find the active effect whose `EffectId` starts with `Enchant_`, the way `UI/GBHUD.cpp` does; clamp to 0..1; if `TotalDuration` is 0, use 1).
  - Not enchanted: `ElementColor` = the gun's own colour `PistolIdleGlow` = (0.02, 1.0, 0.07) (the model's original green), `ImbueRemaining` = 0 (bar dark).
  - Only call `SetVectorParameterValue` / `SetScalarParameterValue` when the value changed (cache the last ones), not every frame.

- The meshes are loaded by path, so the cooker will not find them by reference. Add `+DirectoriesToAlwaysCook=(Path="/Game/Glyphbound/Weapons")` next to the other `DirectoriesToAlwaysCook` lines in `Config/DefaultGame.ini`.

1. The four result lines verbatim, plus the new SMOKE lines.
2. What you changed, with file names.
3. What you saw in the three screenshots, and any tuning value you changed.

5. What a person should check by playing.

## 8. Weapons and items

### Held slots
- The player carries **one gun and one staff.** Never two guns or two staffs.
- Once obtained, the **elemental sword is a special third slot.**
- Switch with the **mouse wheel or Alt**; on gamepad, with a **D-pad arrow** (which one: **TBD**).
- Staff in hand: basic magic attack + the 5 spells. Gun in hand: shoot + aim + reload + the enchant.

### Staffs (medieval, pixel art)
- With a staff in hand, **primary fire = basic magic attack**. The attack **depends on which staff** the player holds, so there is more than one staff.
- Staffs are found in **chests** around the map.
- **A staff that is picked up goes to the inventory** (owner, 2026-11-12). Nothing is dropped on the floor and the staff in hand is not replaced: the player opens the inventory and equips the new one by hand. (Provisional, architect: guns and the sword follow the same rule; the first weapon of each kind goes straight to its empty slot.)
- Staff list and what each basic attack does: **TBD**.

### Guns (cyberpunk, 3D)

244	- Pistol, shotgun, assault rifle.
245	- The **first gun** is dropped by one of the first armed orcs in the future (§4). The **shotgun and the rifle** are dropped later by enemies, picked up from the floor.

# Pistol (source art) — v5

Master Blender file for the cyberpunk pistol. It came from ASSETS as v4 (Tripo task `50e44d0b`, edited there with
Codex and Cursor) and was finished on CENTRAL with the scripts in `Tools/Blender/` (see `Devlog/days/2026-11-12.md`,
ninth block). Older versions were deleted on CENTRAL; ASSETS keeps its own originals.

- `Pistol.blend` — SHA-256 `D571FE3E7EE13AEC8F69868F209489ED674A5AB4974AF218416A14803C5D3F81` (Blender 5.3.0).
  52,893 triangles. 0.97 m long in Blender units: scale on export. Muzzle points to -X; the energy bar is on -Y.
  Trigger: `Trigger_pivot_trial`, frames 1-16. Magazine: `TRIAL_Magazine_Control`, frames 24-72.
- `Textures/` — baked for Unreal by `pistol_prepare_ue.py`: `T_Pistol_BaseColor` (sRGB), `T_Pistol_ORM`
  (R = AO, G = roughness, B = metallic), `T_Pistol_Normal` (DirectX), `T_Pistol_EmissiveMask` (where the body glows
  in the element colour).
- Energy bar `V4_energy_cells`: UV map `ImbueU`, U = 0 at the muzzle end, 1 at the grip end; light cells where
  U < ImbueRemaining.
- Element colour (one mesh, one material parameter): green `(0.02, 1.0, 0.07)`, purple `(0.32, 0.015, 1.0)`
  (linear). The purple .blend was the same file with the other value and was not kept.
- `clean_log.txt` — the regions removed from the atlas and the donor offset of each.

Still to do: FBX export and the UE 5.9 material; lens and reticle; check all 72 frames from the real game camera
(the trigger's saw teeth are accepted only if the player cannot see them).

170	- Small slip: a stray `cat >` with no input in a shell command hung waiting on stdin again; stopped it and wrote the script with the file tool instead. Rule for the scratchpad: write scripts with the file tool, never with an empty `cat >`.
171	
172	## Ninth block: the first 3D pistol arrives from ASSETS, cleaned up in Blender on CENTRAL
173	The ASSETS machine (Codex, then Cursor) built the cyberpunk pistol from a Tripo generation (task `50e44d0b`, Tripo B, about 52,900 triangles in 35 meshes) and sent the unfinished v4 to CENTRAL with a status note: two inherited marks covered with flat grey rectangles, and seven open items (marks, masks, AO, lens, camera check, export). Owner's message (Spanish, translated): "First pistol done, still needs polish." CENTRAL has Blender 5.3.0, so the architect continued here, headless, with scripts kept in `Tools/Blender/`.
174	
175	- **Inventory first** (`pistol_inspect.py`): the note's numbers held (52,893 triangles; trigger and magazine animation 1-72 at 24 fps). New facts: the gun is 0.97 m long in Blender units (to scale on export), the albedo is a Color Ramp of the atlas luminance (near-black to silver), and the glow is a colour key on the atlas (`min(G,B) > 1.35 R` and `> 0.12`).
176	- **Sweep of the whole atlas** in 16 native tiles, then the roughness channel too: 9 more marks besides v4's two (digits on a glowing label, a symbol label, two lines of vertical text, a QR-like block, tiny text, two older flat patches), plus one symbol that lives **only in the roughness channel**. That one was why v4 still showed a smudge on the right-hand silver panel although its colour atlas looked clean. A first-person-like render then showed three more on the face the player sees: dotted columns that stretched faces blow up into text-like smears, and an engraved dotted arc under the dial.
177	- **How they were removed** (`pistol_clean_atlas.py`): seamless (Poisson-style) cloning. For each region a donor block nearby is chosen by matching the ring of pixels around it, in colour and roughness together, then pasted with a harmonic correction so the edges match. The same offset is applied to Color, ORM and Normal, so relief and roughness agree with the colour. Thin text and the glowing label use a smooth harmonic fill instead. Each run was checked by eye on before/after crops and renders, and three rounds were thrown away: an edge penalty that made the v4 patch worse, a donor that brought a dark inset, and a grain donor with vertical streaks. The last old patch uses a smooth fill plus soft noise, its strength measured robustly on its surroundings.
178	- **Ready for Unreal, without touching `Content`** (`pistol_prepare_ue.py`): the Blender-only shader logic baked into plain textures: base colour (the ramp applied), ORM (AO in R, now used), normal flipped to DirectX, and an explicit emissive mask. The energy bar got a second UV map, `ImbueU`, so a UE material can light cells where U < `ImbueRemaining`. Green and purple variants produce the identical cleaned atlas, so one mesh with an element colour parameter covers both.
179	- **Implementer exception:** done by the architect directly, not Muse Spark: the work is a loop of render, look, adjust, and needs someone reading the images.
180	- Not done yet: export to FBX and the UE material (waiting for the owner's go-ahead, as the ASSETS note asks), lens and reticle rebuild, and the check from the real game camera of all 72 animation frames. No claim that no mark is left; the sweep covered colour and roughness, not the normal map tile by tile.
181	- **Where it lives now** (owner, translated: "once the assets are on the central computer they no longer need to stay in shared folders; they become part of the central project, and you can delete old versions"): the master is `Glyphbound/SourceArt/Weapons/Pistol/Pistol.blend` with its baked `Textures/`, outside git like `Content` (only its README is tracked, with hashes and conventions). The shared v4 copy, the work folder, review crops and renders were deleted on CENTRAL; ASSETS keeps its own originals. The purple .blend was dropped: same mesh, only the element colour differs, which becomes a material parameter in UE (both values are in the README).
182	- **Blender MCP: not installed, for now.** The owner suggested it. Architect's call: the headless scripts already do the job and they are reproducible and versioned, which counts for Glass Box. The MCP would need a Blender window open with an add-on, plus one more server. The remaining work (export, UE material, camera check) happens mostly in Unreal. To revisit if a step needs interactive modelling (the lens rebuild might).
183	- Screenshots: `media/2026-11-12/12a_pistol_v4_plusY.png` (v4: smudge on the silver panel), `12b_pistol_v5_plusY.png` (v5: gone), `12c_pistol_v5_rear.png` (the face the player sees), `12d_pistol_v5_front34.png`. Renders in Blender EEVEE with neutral studio light, not in Unreal.
184	
185	## Ninth block: the weapon tree, reorganized
186	The owner brought a list of perks and a sketch of the weapon tree (made with an AI assistant, in Spanish): Rapid Reload, Precision Recovery, Arcane Conduit and a pistol specialization, Deadeye, plus a layout with a handling branch, a precision branch and the three weapon specializations on one row so no gun is favored. The owner's own edits to that proposal (translated): "Precision Recovery heals a fixed 3% of max health, but the internal cooldown goes down with the ranks: 6 / 5 / 4. Deadeye: +0.25x damage per rank." The proposal also warned that a heal per head hit (or per shotgun pellet) would mean near-unlimited healing in a horde game; that became the rule: one heal per enemy death, only when the killing blow is a weak-point hit.
187	
188	- Architect: GDD v0.24 and the brief `Prompts/feedback9_weapon_tree.md` (layout table, data keys, two pure functions, smoke checks). Provisional: the prerequisites the sketch did not draw (Steady Grip under Quick Trigger, Arcane Conduit under Marksman), Steady Grip now also lowering yaw recoil.
189	- Muse Spark implemented it in one run: all green, 36 tests, new smoke lines (`precision recovery healed=3.0`, `cooldown healed=0.0`, `rapid reload pistol=0.84`, `arcane conduit buildup=19.50 base=15.00`). Its choice for the death hook: the global damage-dealt event, which carries the killing blow and its instigator; a dead target takes no more damage, so a shotgun's other pellets cannot heal again. Read and accepted by the architect.
190	- Architect fix after looking at the smoke screenshot `12_weapon_tree`: links from Heavy Rounds to the bottom row ran diagonally through the translucent boxes in between; links that skip rows are now drawn as elbows down the parent's column.
191	
192	## Design decisions
193	All taken by the architect; the owner asked not to be consulted on engineering. The provisional gameplay rules and numbers that had to be invented are listed in GDD section 18 for the owner to confirm or change.
194	
195	- **C++ only, built from the blank template.** The first-person template was not used: the jam asks for gameplay beyond Epic's templates, and AI agents handle C++ text far better than Blueprint graphs.
196	- **No Gameplay Ability System.** Considered (the GDD lists it as a candidate) and rejected: heavy boilerplate and asset setup for a 4-day jam. Replaced by three small pieces we fully control: one stat system (base value from data + stacked modifiers), one damage function, one status-effect component. Skill-tree nodes, armor, slows, potions, air passives and the weapon enchant are all "a named group of modifiers".
197	- **All gameplay numbers in JSON under `Content/Data`, shipped as loose files.** Git only carries text in this team, AI agents edit text reliably, and the owner can retune a packaged build with a text editor. `gb.ReloadData` reloads while playing.
198	- **Spells = data + a behavior class.** Each parameter has `Base / Min / Max / ScaledBy` (none, QTE power, QTE reach). Eight behaviors cover the nine active spells and the enchant; a new spell that fits a behavior is one JSON entry.
199	- **No binary assets needed to run.** The test arena, input actions and placeholders are built in C++; placeholder pixel art is rows of text turned into textures at runtime. The whole game is reviewable as text in git.
200	- **HUD drawn with the canvas, not widgets.** The two skins (90s RPG with the staff, cyberpunk with a gun) are two style structs.
201	- **Death keeps what was collected** (after the review): back to the checkpoint's place with full health, mana and ammo; nothing owned is rolled back.
202	- **Modifier keys by weapon type** (`Weapon.Gun.*`), added after the review found the gun enchant also buffed the staff.
203	- **Routing of work between models** (owner's rule): parallel work to Claude subagents, one-batch-at-a-time work to Muse Spark, reviews to Codex.
204	- **Exceptions to "the implementer is Muse Spark"**, with the reason: the project scaffold, the header contracts and the build / test / smoke scripts were written by the architect directly (they are the architecture and its verification); two one-line fixes and the sprite palette script were also direct (smaller than the prompt that would describe them).
205	
206	## Assets created
207	| Asset | Tool (AI or manual) | Prompt or source | License | Machine |
208	|---|---|---|---|---|
209	| 36 placeholder pixel sprites (`Content/Data/Sprites.json`, rows of text) | AI (Claude Opus 5.5 subagent "UI") | Architect's task brief in the session log | Own work | CENTRAL |
210	| Cyberpunk pistol v1-v4 (mesh, 2K PBR atlas, trigger and magazine animation, green and purple element variants) | AI: Tripo (task `50e44d0b`, kept) and Meshy (compared, not kept); edited in Blender 5.2.3 / 5.3.0 by Codex and Cursor | Owner's reference image; full trace on ASSETS (`reports/01_generation_manifest.md`) | AI-generated during the jam; inherited marks being removed | ASSETS |
211	| Cyberpunk pistol v5 (marks removed from colour, roughness and normal; UE textures baked; `ImbueU` UV on the energy bar) | Blender 5.3.0 headless, scripts in `Tools/Blender/` (Claude Opus 5.5) | ASSETS v4 | As above | CENTRAL |
212	
213	No third-party assets. Engine content used: the basic shapes and engine materials that ship with UE 5.9.
214	
215	## Problems and solutions
216	- **Trimming plugins did not speed up a warm Editor boot.** We expected a gain; measured, there is none worth the name. Mounted plugins went from 315 to 160, warm boot stayed around 10-11 s. The cost of a warm boot is not in the plugin count. We keep the trimmed list (fewer modules to load and cook) and spent no more time on it.
217	- **Screenshots arrive late.** The engine captures a screenshot a few frames after the request, so in the first smoke run a shot of "the future" showed the inventory that opened right after. The script now leaves a full second after each shot.
218	- Everything else is in "Where the AI failed" above.
219	
220	## Screenshots / clips
221	All taken by the scripted run (`gb.Smoke`) of the second packaged build, not by a person playing.
222	- `media/2026-11-12/1_past_staff.png`: the past. Staff in hand, 90s RPG HUD, an ice wall just cast: a 3D block with a pixel tile, like the stone walls and floor of the arena.
223	- `media/2026-11-12/2_past_gun.png`: pixel-art hands holding the 3D pistol, cyberpunk HUD, the gun enchanted with fire, and a floating damage number.
224	- `media/2026-11-12/9_shield.png`: the summoned ice shield, raised with the Block key.
225	- `media/2026-11-12/3_future_gun.png`: the same place in the future (dark, neon).
226	- `media/2026-11-12/4_inventory.png`, `5_skills.png`: inventory and both skill trees, each tree in its own style.
227	- `media/2026-11-12/5b_skills_reset.png` (fourth build): the skill trees right after "Reset skills": the node is back at 0/3, the points are back and the button is greyed.
228	- `media/2026-11-12/10_ground_spells.png` (sixth build): the lightning rune drawn flat over its whole area, and the ice floor cast after it covering the overlap cleanly.
229	- `media/2026-11-12/12_weapon_tree.png` (eleventh build): the reorganized weapon tree (handling and precision branches, specializations on the bottom row, elbow links), with the "+3 health" Precision Recovery message from the smoke run.
230	- `media/2026-11-12/6_qte.png`: the spell QTE: key sequence, time bar, power and reach.
231	- `media/2026-11-12/7_death.png`, `8_respawn.png`: death screen and the respawn at the portal, keeping the learned spells.

251	Unreal Engine 5.9.0, Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.2, Claude Opus 5.5; Opus 5.5 is also the second architect chat), OpenCode (Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor), Codex CLI (GPT Sol 6.1), Unreal Editor MCP server (boot measurements only), git, Blender 5.2.3 and 5.3.0, Tripo (CLI 0.11.2), Meshy, Cursor.

For each region a donor block nearby is chosen by matching the ring of pixels around it, in colour and roughness together, then pasted with a harmonic correction so the edges match. The same offset is applied to Color, ORM and Normal, so relief and roughness agree with the colour. Thin text and the glowing label use a smooth harmonic fill instead. Each run was checked by eye on before/after crops and renders, and three rounds were thrown away: an edge penalty that made the v4 patch worse, a donor that brought a dark inset, and a grain donor with vertical streaks. The last old patch uses a smooth fill plus soft noise, its strength measured robustly on its surroundings.
- **Ready for Unreal, without touching `Content`** (`pistol_prepare_ue.py`): the Blender-only shader logic baked into plain textures: base colour (the ramp applied), ORM (AO in R, now used), normal flipped to DirectX, and an explicit emissive mask. The energy bar got a second UV map, `ImbueU`, so a UE material can light cells where U < `ImbueRemaining`. Green and purple variants produce the identical cleaned atlas, so one mesh with an element colour parameter covers both.
- **Implementer exception:** done by the architect directly, not Muse Spark: the work is a loop of render, look, adjust, and needs someone reading the images.
- Not done yet: export to FBX and the UE material (waiting for the owner's go-ahead, as the ASSETS note asks), lens and reticle rebuild, and the check from the real game camera of all 72 animation frames. No claim that no mark is left; the sweep covered colour and roughness, not the normal map tile by tile.
- **Where it lives now** (owner, translated: "once the assets are on the central computer they no longer need to stay in shared folders; they become part of the central project, and you can delete old versions"): the master is `Glyphbound/SourceArt/Weapons/Pistol/Pistol.blend` with its baked `Textures/`, outside git like `Content` (only its README is tracked, with hashes and conventions). The shared v4 copy, the work folder, review crops and renders were deleted on CENTRAL; ASSETS keeps its own originals. The purple .blend was dropped: same mesh, only the element colour differs, which becomes a material parameter in UE (both values are in the README).
- **Blender MCP: not installed, for now.** The owner suggested it. Architect's call: the headless scripts already do the job and they are reproducible and versioned, which counts for Glass Box. The MCP would need a Blender window open with an add-on, plus one more server. The remaining work (export, UE material, camera check) happens mostly in Unreal. To revisit if a step needs interactive modelling (the lens rebuild might).
- Screenshots: `media/2026-11-12/12a_pistol_v4_plusY.png` (v4: smudge on the silver panel), `12b_pistol_v5_plusY.png` (v5: gone), `12c_pistol_v5_rear.png` (the face the player sees), `12d_pistol_v5_front34.png`. Renders in Blender EEVEE with neutral studio light, not in Unreal.

## Ninth block: the weapon tree, reorganized
The owner brought a list of perks and a sketch of the weapon tree (made with an AI assistant, in Spanish): Rapid Reload, Precision Recovery, Arcane Conduit and a pistol specialization, Deadeye, plus a layout with a handling branch, a precision branch and the three weapon specializations on one row so no gun is favored. The owner's own edits to that proposal (translated): "Precision Recovery heals a fixed 3% of max health, but the internal cooldown goes down with the ranks: 6 / 5 / 4. Deadeye: +0.25x damage per rank." The proposal also warned that a heal per head hit (or per shotgun pellet) would mean near-unlimited healing in a horde game; that became the rule: one heal per enemy death, only when the killing blow is a weak-point hit.

- Architect: GDD v0.24 and the brief `Prompts/feedback9_weapon_tree.md` (layout table, data keys, two pure functions, smoke checks). Provisional: the prerequisites the sketch did not draw (Steady Grip under Quick Trigger, Arcane Conduit under Marksman), Steady Grip now also lowering yaw recoil.
- Muse Spark implemented it in one run: all green, 36 tests, new smoke lines (`precision recovery healed=3.0`, `cooldown healed=0.0`, `rapid reload pistol=0.84`, `arcane conduit buildup=19.50 base=15.00`). Its choice for the death hook: the global damage-dealt event, which carries the killing blow and its instigator; a dead target takes no more damage, so a shotgun's other pellets cannot heal again. Read and accepted by the architect.
- Architect fix after looking at the smoke screenshot `12_weapon_tree`: links from Heavy Rounds to the bottom row ran diagonally through the translucent boxes in between; links that skip rows are now drawn as elbows down the parent's column.

## Design decisions
All taken by the architect; the owner asked not to be consulted on engineering. The provisional gameplay rules and numbers that had to be invented are listed in GDD section 18 for the owner to confirm or change.

- **C++ only, built from the blank template.** The first-person template was not used: the jam asks for gameplay beyond Epic's templates, and AI agents handle C++ text far better than Blueprint graphs.
- **No Gameplay Ability System.** Considered (the GDD lists it as a candidate) and rejected: heavy boilerplate and asset setup for a 4-day jam. Replaced by three small pieces we fully control: one stat system (base value from data + stacked modifiers), one damage function, one status-effect component. Skill-tree nodes, armor, slows, potions, air passives and the weapon enchant are all "a named group of modifiers".
- **All gameplay numbers in JSON under `Content/Data`, shipped as loose files.** Git only carries text in this team, AI agents edit text reliably, and the owner can retune a packaged build with a text editor. `gb.ReloadData` reloads while playing.
- **Spells = data + a behavior class.** Each parameter has `Base / Min / Max / ScaledBy` (none, QTE power, QTE reach). Eight behaviors cover the nine active spells and the enchant; a new spell that fits a behavior is one JSON entry.
- **No binary assets needed to run.** The test arena, input actions and placeholders are built in C++; placeholder pixel art is rows of text turned into textures at runtime. The whole game is reviewable as text in git.
- **HUD drawn with the canvas, not widgets.** The two skins (90s RPG with the staff, cyberpunk with a gun) are two style structs.
- **Death keeps what was collected** (after the review): back to the checkpoint's place with full health, mana and ammo; nothing owned is rolled back.
- **Modifier keys by weapon type** (`Weapon.Gun.*`), added after the review found the gun enchant also buffed the staff.
- **Routing of work between models** (owner's rule): parallel work to Claude subagents, one-batch-at-a-time work to Muse Spark, reviews to Codex.
- **Exceptions to "the implementer is Muse Spark"**, with the reason: the project scaffold, the header contracts and the build / test / smoke scripts were written by the architect directly (they are the architecture and its verification); two one-line fixes and the sprite palette script were also direct (smaller than the prompt that would describe them).

## Assets created
| Asset | Tool (AI or manual) | Prompt or source | License | Machine |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 36 placeholder pixel sprites (`Content/Data/Sprites.json`, rows of text) | AI (Claude Opus 5.5 subagent "UI") | Architect's task brief in the session log | Own work | CENTRAL |
| Cyberpunk pistol v1-v4 (mesh, 2K PBR atlas, trigger and magazine animation, green and purple element variants) | AI: Tripo (task `50e44d0b`, kept) and Meshy (compared, not kept); edited in Blender 5.2.3 / 5.3.0 by Codex and Cursor | Owner's reference image; full trace on ASSETS (`reports/01_generation_manifest.md`) | AI-generated during the jam; inherited marks being removed | ASSETS |
| Cyberpunk pistol v5 (marks removed from colour, roughness and normal; UE textures baked; `ImbueU` UV on the energy bar) | Blender 5.3.0 headless, scripts in `Tools/Blender/` (Claude Opus 5.5) | ASSETS v4 | As above | CENTRAL |

No third-party assets. Engine content used: the basic shapes and engine materials that ship with UE 5.9.

## Problems and solutions
- **Trimming plugins did not speed up a warm Editor boot.** We expected a gain; measured, there is none worth the name. Mounted plugins went from 315 to 160, warm boot stayed around 10-11 s. The cost of a warm boot is not in the plugin count. We keep the trimmed list (fewer modules to load and cook) and spent no more time on it.
- **Screenshots arrive late.** The engine captures a screenshot a few frames after the request, so in the first smoke run a shot of "the future" showed the inventory that opened right after. The script now leaves a full second after each shot.
- Everything else is in "Where the AI failed" above.

## Screenshots / clips
All taken by the scripted run (`gb.Smoke`) of the second packaged build, not by a person playing.
- `media/2026-11-12/1_past_staff.png`: the past. Staff in hand, 90s RPG HUD, an ice wall just cast: a 3D block with a pixel tile, like the stone walls and floor of the arena.
- `media/2026-11-12/2_past_gun.png`: pixel-art hands holding the 3D pistol, cyberpunk HUD, the gun enchanted with fire, and a floating damage number.
- `media/2026-11-12/9_shield.png`: the summoned ice shield, raised with the Block key.
- `media/2026-11-12/3_future_gun.png`: the same place in the future (dark, neon).
- `media/2026-11-12/4_inventory.png`, `5_skills.png`: inventory and both skill trees, each tree in its own style.
- `media/2026-11-12/5b_skills_reset.png` (fourth build): the skill trees right after "Reset skills": the node is back at 0/3, the points are back and the button is greyed.
- `media/2026-11-12/10_ground_spells.png` (sixth build): the lightning rune drawn flat over its whole area, and the ice floor cast after it covering the overlap cleanly.
- `media/2026-11-12/12_weapon_tree.png` (eleventh build): the reorganized weapon tree (handling and precision branches, specializations on the bottom row, elbow links), with the "+3 health" Precision Recovery message from the smoke run.
- `media/2026-11-12/6_qte.png`: the spell QTE: key sequence, time bar, power and reach.
- `media/2026-11-12/7_death.png`, `8_respawn.png`: death screen and the respawn at the portal, keeping the learned spells.

## Numbers of the day
- Editor boot, `Total Editor Startup Time` from the log (same machine, same code, empty startup map):

| Plugin set | Mounted plugins | Cold (first boot) | Warm boots |
|---|---|---|---|
| Default + `AllToolsets` (baseline) | 315 | 37.9 s | 10.97 s, 10.96 s |
| Trimmed (18 toolsets, 103 defaults off; later 102, see above) | 160 | 16.3 s (first boot after the change) | 10.09 s, 11.15 s |

- Code: 103 files, about 17,500 lines; 11 JSON data files.
- First full compile of all the parallel work: 3 errors.
- Tests: 26 pure-logic tests (24 after the second block), 0.43 s of test time, 15-25 s wall time with the Editor boot.
- Smoke run: 31 steps, 40-48 s wall time.
- Second block (play-test notes): 56 files changed, 4,428 lines added, 0 compile errors on the first build, 4 review findings; from the owner's message to the second packaged build in one working session.
- Build times: first build of the empty module 55 s; incremental builds 2-26 s.
- Package: `TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip`, **245.4 MB** after the second block (245.3 MB the first time; the jam asks for under 1 GB), built in 51-56 s. The packaged exe passes the same scripted run, reading the JSON data as loose files next to it, with the generated material and the runtime navmesh working.
- Agent sessions / prompts / external agent runs / MCP calls / commits: see `2026-11-12_DRAFT.md`.

## Tools used so far (for the submission's "Tools you used" field)
Unreal Engine 5.9.0, Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.2, Claude Opus 5.5; Opus 5.5 is also the second architect chat), OpenCode (Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor), Codex CLI (GPT Sol 6.1), Unreal Editor MCP server (boot measurements only), git, Blender 5.2.3 and 5.3.0, Tripo (CLI 0.11.2), Meshy, Cursor.

## Plan for tomorrow
- A person plays the second packaged build first, and their notes decide the order of everything else. To check by hand: mouse in menus, the Block key, equipping a second staff from the inventory, enemies around cover, falling off the map, damage numbers.
- Tune by playing: movement feel, mouse gesture sensitivity in the QTE, gun viewmodel size, spell numbers.
- GDD day 2: gamepad pass, enemy behavior and one real wave, consumables in play, QTE second version, DLSS plugin check for the NVIDIA award.
- Replace placeholders as art arrives from the other machines.

## Tenth block: the pistol goes into the game
Owner's answer to "export the pistol to Unreal and replace the placeholder?" (Spanish, translated): "Go ahead." GDD v0.25.

- **Export from Blender** (`Tools/Blender/pistol_export_fbx.py`, architect): four static meshes instead of one animated file, because the game animates the moving parts in code: body, trigger (pivot on its hinge), magazine (pivot at its centre) and energy bar (alone, so its second UV map `ImbueU` reaches Unreal as UV channel 1). Rest pose, turned so the muzzle points to Unreal's +X, origin at the hand point. The old lens faces (transparent in Blender) were dropped. The offsets and motions the code needs are written to `export_report.json`. Two small listing scripts (`pistol_list_objects.py`, `pistol_list_materials.py`) read the objects, the animation keys and the material values first.
- **Import into Unreal without the Editor open** (`Tools/Jam/Import-Pistol.ps1` + `import_pistol.py`, architect): the same pattern as `make_materials.py`, because `Content/` is not in git. It imports the four FBX files and the four baked textures, builds four materials from text (`M_GunSolid` with one instance per Blender material and its PBR values copied, `M_PistolAtlas` with the baked atlas, `M_GunEnergy` for the bar, `M_GunGlass` for the sight pane), assigns every slot and fails if a slot is left without a material. It checks the result in Unreal: bounds (the muzzle really is at +X and the bar on the side the camera sees) and the bar's UV channel 1 spanning 0 to 1. Four rounds to get it green: two API calls that do not exist in a commandlet, and a UV count that always read 0 there, replaced by reading the UV values themselves.
- **Code** (`Prompts/feedback10_pistol_viewmodel.md`, Muse Spark, one run): a `ViewModel` field in `Weapons.json` (only the pistol uses it; shotgun and rifle keep their shapes), the four parts attached at scale 0.3, the trigger pulled on each shot, the magazine sliding out and back in with the reload progress, and the glow: the gun's own green when not enchanted; the element colour plus the bar showing the enchant time left while enchanted. If the meshes are missing (another machine without `Content/`) it logs one warning and builds the placeholder. The weapons folder is added to the always-cooked directories. Smoke checks: `pistol viewmodel meshes=4 mids=18`, `pistol magazine offset=27.0` (full out at mid-reload), `pistol glow element=Fire imbue=0.96`. Read and accepted by the architect.
- **Implementer:** the export and import are Editor and art tooling, done by the architect (same reason as the ninth block); the game code went to Muse Spark. From here on, in this chat, the owner set Claude Sonnet 5.5 (High effort) as the implementer instead of Muse Spark (owner's rule for this chat only).
- What a person must check by playing: the trigger flick on each shot, the magazine during a reload (in the smoke shot at mid-reload it is below the bottom edge of the screen), the bar draining during an enchant, and the size and placement of the gun (it fills the lower right; the scale is one constant in `GBGun.cpp`).
- Screenshots: `media/2026-11-12/13a_pistol_hip.png` (not enchanted, green glow) and `13c_pistol_enchanted.png` (fire enchant, orange glow, bar lit).

All taken by the architect;

- **Export from Blender** (`Tools/Blender/pistol_export_fbx.py`, architect): four static meshes instead of one animated file, because the game animates the moving parts in code: body, trigger (pivot on its hinge), magazine (pivot at its centre) and energy bar (alone, so its second UV map `ImbueU` reaches Unreal as UV channel 1). Rest pose, turned so the muzzle points to Unreal's +X, origin at the hand point. The old lens faces (transparent in Blender) were dropped. The offsets and motions the code needs are written to `export_report.json`. Two small listing scripts (`pistol_list_objects.py`, `pistol_list_materials.py`) read the objects, the animation keys and the material values first.
- **Import into Unreal without the Editor open** (`Tools/Jam/Import-Pistol.ps1` + `import_pistol.py`, architect): the same pattern as `make_materials.py`, because `Content/` is not in git. It imports the four FBX files and the four baked textures, builds four materials from text (`M_GunSolid` with one instance per Blender material and its PBR values copied, `M_PistolAtlas` with the baked atlas, `M_GunEnergy` for the bar, `M_GunGlass` for the sight pane), assigns every slot and fails if a slot is left without a material. It checks the result in Unreal: bounds (the muzzle really is at +X and the bar on the side the camera sees) and the bar's UV channel 1 spanning 0 to 1. Four rounds to get it green: two API calls that do not exist in a commandlet, and a UV count that always read 0 there, replaced by reading the UV values themselves.
- **Code** (`Prompts/feedback10_pistol_viewmodel.md`, Muse Spark, one run): a `ViewModel` field in `Weapons.json` (only the pistol uses it; shotgun and rifle keep their shapes), the four parts attached at scale 0.3, the trigger pulled on each shot, the magazine sliding out and back in with the reload progress, and the glow: the gun's own green when not enchanted; the element colour plus the bar showing the enchant time left while enchanted. If the meshes are missing (another machine without `Content/`) it logs one warning and builds the placeholder. The weapons folder is added to the always-cooked directories. Smoke checks: `pistol viewmodel meshes=4 mids=18`, `pistol magazine offset=27.0` (full out at mid-reload), `pistol glow element=Fire imbue=0.96`. Read and accepted by the architect.
- **Implementer:** the export and import are Editor and art tooling, done by the architect (same reason as the ninth block); the game code went to Muse Spark. From here on, in this chat, the owner set Claude Sonnet 5.5 (High effort) as the implementer instead of Muse Spark (owner's rule for this chat only).
- What a person must check by playing: the trigger flick on each shot, the magazine during a reload (in the smoke shot at mid-reload it is below the bottom edge of the screen), the bar draining during an enchant, and the size and placement of the gun (it fills the lower right; the scale is one constant in `GBGun.cpp`).
- Screenshots: `media/2026-11-12/13a_pistol_hip.png` (not enchanted, green glow) and `13c_pistol_enchanted.png` (fire enchant, orange glow, bar lit).

Four rounds to get it green: two API calls that do not exist in a commandlet, and a UV count that always read 0 there, replaced by reading the UV values themselves.

- **Code** (`Prompts/feedback10_pistol_viewmodel.md`, Muse Spark, one run): a `ViewModel` field in `Weapons.json` (only the pistol uses it; shotgun and rifle keep their shapes), the four parts attached at scale 0.3, the trigger pulled on each shot, the magazine sliding out and back in with the reload progress, and the glow: the gun's own green when not enchanted; the element colour plus the bar showing the enchant time left while enchanted. If the meshes are missing (another machine without `Content/`) it logs one warning and builds the placeholder. The weapons folder is added to the always-cooked directories. Smoke checks: `pistol viewmodel meshes=4 mids=18`, `pistol magazine offset=27.0` (full out at mid-reload), `pistol glow element=Fire imbue=0.96`. Read and accepted by the architect.

+- Twelfth package: `TeamTBD_Glyphbound.zip` 251 MB (was 245 MB; the pistol adds about 6 MB). The packaged exe passes the same scripted run with `meshes=4`, so the cooker picked up the meshes loaded by path. First packaging attempt failed only because the project path was relative (UAT needs it absolute).

- **Implementer:** the export and import are Editor and art tooling, done by the architect (same reason as the ninth block); the game code went to Muse Spark. From here on, in this chat, the owner set Claude Sonnet 5.5 (High effort) as the implementer instead of Muse Spark (owner's rule for this chat only).

- What a person must check by playing: the trigger flick on each shot, the magazine during a reload (in the smoke shot at mid-reload it is below the bottom edge of the screen), the bar draining during an enchant, and the size and placement of the gun (it fills the lower right; the scale is one constant in `GBGun.cpp`).
- Screenshots: `media/2026-11-12/13a_pistol_hip.png` (not enchanted, green glow) and `13c_pistol_enchanted.png` (fire enchant, orange glow, bar lit).

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Prepares the cleaned pistol for Unreal 5.9 without touching the UE project:
#  1. Bakes the Blender-only shader logic of the atlas material into plain textures:
#     - T_Pistol_BaseColor (sRGB): the Color Ramp of the luminance that the Blender material used as albedo
#       (so UE does not depend on the ramp),
#     - T_Pistol_ORM (linear): R = AO, G = roughness, B = metallic (UE's usual packing; AO now gets used),
#     - T_Pistol_Normal (linear, DirectX/UE convention: green flipped from the OpenGL source),
#     - T_Pistol_EmissiveMask (linear, grayscale): where the atlas glows in the element color
#       (Blender rule: m = min(G, B); glow = 0.65 if m > 1.35 R and m > 0.12).
#  2. Adds a second UV map "ImbueU" to the energy bar: U goes 0..1 along X like the Generated X the Blender
#     material used, so the UE material can light cells where U < ImbueRemaining.
#  3. Saves the .blend in place.
# Usage: blender -b <cleaned.blend> --python pistol_prepare_ue.py -- <export_dir>
import bpy, sys, os
import numpy as np

argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
out_dir = argv[0]
os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)

def to_linear(c):
    return np.where(c <= 0.04045, c / 12.92, ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4)

def to_srgb(c):
    c = np.clip(c, 0, 1)
    return np.where(c <= 0.0031308, c * 12.92, 1.055 * np.power(c, 1 / 2.4) - 0.055)

def img(prefix):
    im = next(i for i in bpy.data.images if i.name.startswith(prefix))
    w, h = im.size
    return im, np.array(im.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4)

def save(name, arr, colorspace):
    h, w = arr.shape[:2]
    out = bpy.data.images.new(name, w, h, alpha=False)
    out.colorspace_settings.name = colorspace
    out.pixels.foreach_set(np.ascontiguousarray(arr).ravel())
    out.filepath_raw = os.path.join(out_dir, name + ".png")
    out.file_format = "PNG"
    out.save()
    print("WROTE", out.filepath_raw)

mat = next(m for m in bpy.data.materials if m.name.startswith("tripo_material_"))
ramp = next(n for n in mat.node_tree.nodes if n.bl_idname == "ShaderNodeValToRGB").color_ramp
(p0, c0), (p1, c1) = [(e.position, np.array(e.color[:3])) for e in ramp.elements]

_, C = img("Color_")
_, O = img("ORM_")
_, N = img("NormalGL_")
lin = to_linear(C[..., :3])                       # the shader samples the sRGB atlas as linear
lum = lin @ np.array([0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722], np.float32)
t = np.clip((lum - p0) / (p1 - p0), 0, 1)[..., None]
albedo_lin = c0 + (c1 - c0) * t                   # linear ramp between the two stops
base = np.ones_like(C)
base[..., :3] = to_srgb(albedo_lin)
save("T_Pistol_BaseColor", base, "sRGB")

m = np.minimum(lin[..., 1], lin[..., 2])
glow = ((m > 1.35 * lin[..., 0]) & (m > 0.12)).astype(np.float32)
mask = np.ones_like(C)
mask[..., 0] = mask[..., 1] = mask[..., 2] = glow
save("T_Pistol_EmissiveMask", mask, "Non-Color")
print("EMISSIVE_PIXELS", int(glow.sum()))

orm = O.copy()
orm[..., 3] = 1
save("T_Pistol_ORM", orm, "Non-Color")

nrm = N.copy()
nrm[..., 1] = 1.0 - nrm[..., 1]                   # OpenGL -> DirectX
nrm[..., 3] = 1
save("T_Pistol_Normal", nrm, "Non-Color")

# second UV map on the energy bar: U = position along X (0 = muzzle end, 1 = grip end), V = 0.5
bar = bpy.data.objects["V4_energy_cells"]
me = bar.data
uv = me.uv_layers.get("ImbueU") or me.uv_layers.new(name="ImbueU")
xs = [v.co.x for v in me.vertices]
x0, x1 = min(xs), max(xs)
for loop in me.loops:
    x = me.vertices[loop.vertex_index].co.x
    uv.data[loop.index].uv = ((x - x0) / (x1 - x0), 0.5)
print("IMBUE_UV", bar.name, "x range", round(x0, 4), round(x1, 4), "uv layers", [l.name for l in me.uv_layers])

bpy.ops.wm.save_mainfile(compress=True)
print("SAVED", bpy.data.filepath)

#     - T_Pistol_BaseColor (sRGB): the Color Ramp of the luminance that the Blender material used as albedo
#       (so UE does not depend on the ramp),
#     - T_Pistol_ORM (linear): R = AO, G = roughness, B = metallic (UE's usual packing; AO now gets used),
#     - T_Pistol_Normal (linear, DirectX/UE convention: green flipped from the OpenGL source),
#     - T_Pistol_EmissiveMask (linear, grayscale): where the atlas glows in the element color
#       (Blender rule: m = min(G, B); glow = 0.65 if m > 1.35 R and m > 0.12).
#  2. Adds a second UV map "ImbueU" to the energy bar: U goes 0..1 along X like the Generated X the Blender
#     material used, so the UE material can light cells where U < ImbueRemaining.
#  3. Saves the .blend in place.
# Usage: blender -b <cleaned.blend> --python pistol_prepare_ue.py -- <export_dir>
import bpy, sys, os
import numpy as np

argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
out_dir = argv[0]
os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)

def to_linear(c):
    return np.where(c <= 0.04045, c / 12.92, ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4)

def to_srgb(c):
    c = np.clip(c, 0, 1)
    return np.where(c <= 0.0031308, c * 12.92, 1.055 * np.power(c, 1 / 2.4) - 0.055)

def img(prefix):
    im = next(i for i in bpy.data.images if i.name.startswith(prefix))
    w, h = im.size
    return im, np.array(im.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4)

def save(name, arr, colorspace):
    h, w = arr.shape[:2]
    out = bpy.data.images.new(name, w, h, alpha=False)
    out.colorspace_settings.name = colorspace
    out.pixels.foreach_set(np.ascontiguousarray(arr).ravel())
    out.filepath_raw = os.path.join(out_dir, name + ".png")
    out.file_format = "PNG"
    out.save()
    print("WROTE", out.filepath_raw)

mat = next(m for m in bpy.data.materials if m.name.startswith("tripo_material_"))
ramp = next(n for n in mat.node_tree.nodes if n.bl_idname == "ShaderNodeValToRGB").color_ramp
(p0, c0), (p1, c1) = [(e.position, np.array(e.color[:3])) for e in ramp.elements]

_, C = img("Color_")
_, O = img("ORM_")
_, N = img("NormalGL_")
lin = to_linear(C[..., :3])                       # the shader samples the sRGB atlas as linear
lum = lin @ np.array([0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722], np.float32)
t = np.clip((lum - p0) / (p1 - p0), 0, 1)[..., None]
albedo_lin = c0 + (c1 - c0) * t                   # linear ramp between the two stops
base = np.ones_like(C)
base[..., :3] = to_srgb(albedo_lin)
save("T_Pistol_BaseColor", base, "sRGB")

m = np.minimum(lin[..., 1], lin[..., 2])
glow = ((m > 1.35 * lin[..., 0]) & (m > 0.12)).astype(np.float32)
mask = np.ones_like(C)
mask[..., 0] = mask[..., 1] = mask[..., 2] = glow
save("T_Pistol_EmissiveMask", mask, "Non-Color")
print("EMISSIVE_PIXELS", int(glow.sum()))

orm = O.copy()
orm[..., 3] = 1
save("T_Pistol_ORM", orm, "Non-Color")

nrm = N.copy()
nrm[..., 1] = 1.0 - nrm[..., 1]                   # OpenGL -> DirectX
nrm[..., 3] = 1
save("T_Pistol_Normal", nrm, "Non-Color")

# second UV map on the energy bar: U = position along X (0 = muzzle end, 1 = grip end), V = 0.5
bar = bpy.data.objects["V4_energy_cells"]
me = bar.data
created = me.uv_layers.get("ImbueU") is None
uv = me.uv_layers.get("ImbueU") or me.uv_layers.new(name="ImbueU")
xs = [v.co.x for v in me.vertices]
x0, x1 = min(xs), max(xs)
for loop in me.loops:
    x = me.vertices[loop.vertex_index].co.x
    uv.data[loop.index].uv = ((x - x0) / (x1 - x0), 0.5)
print("IMBUE_UV", bar.name, "x range", round(x0, 4), round(x1, 4), "uv layers", [l.name for l in me.uv_layers])

bpy.ops.wm.save_mainfile(compress=True)
print("SAVED", bpy.data.filepath)

<#
Import-Pistol.ps1 - Imports the cyberpunk pistol (meshes, textures, materials) from Glyphbound/SourceArt into
/Game/Glyphbound/Weapons/Pistol with the Editor's Python commandlet (Tools/Jam/import_pistol.py).
Content is not in git: run this on CENTRAL after the Blender export changes. The Editor must be closed.

Usage:
  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Import-Pistol.ps1
Output: the script's lines, the error lines of the log, OK or FAILED. Exit code 0 = imported and saved.
#>
param(
    [string]$Project = (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..\..\Glyphbound\Glyphbound.uproject'),
    [string]$EngineDir = 'C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.9',
    [int]$TimeoutSeconds = 900
)
$Project = (Resolve-Path $Project).Path
$projDir = Split-Path $Project -Parent
$script = (Resolve-Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'import_pistol.py')).Path
$exe = Join-Path $EngineDir 'Engine\Binaries\Win64\UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe'
if (-not (Test-Path $exe)) { Write-Host "No editor at $exe"; exit 2 }

$stamp = [DateTime]::UtcNow.ToString('yyyyMMdd-HHmmss')
$logDir = Join-Path $projDir 'Saved\Logs'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $logDir | Out-Null
$log = Join-Path $logDir "import_pistol_$stamp.log"

# Materials compile here, so the commandlet needs a renderer (no -NullRHI).
$argList = @("`"$Project`"", '-run=pythonscript', "-script=`"$script`"", "-abslog=`"$log`"",
    '-AllowCommandletRendering', '-unattended', '-nopause', '-nosplash', '-nosound', '-nocrashreports')

$sw = [Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
$p = Start-Process -FilePath $exe -ArgumentList $argList -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden
$timedOut = -not $p.WaitForExit($TimeoutSeconds * 1000)
if ($timedOut) {
    Write-Host "TIMEOUT after $TimeoutSeconds s: stopping the commandlet."
    Stop-Process -Id $p.Id -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}
$sw.Stop()

if (-not (Test-Path $log)) { Write-Host "No log at $log (exit $($p.ExitCode))"; exit 2 }
$lines = Get-Content $log -Encoding UTF8
$ours = @($lines | Where-Object { $_ -match 'import_pistol:' })
$errors = @($lines | Where-Object { $_ -match 'LogPython: Error|import_pistol: ERROR|Traceback|Fatal error|Assertion failed|Unhandled Exception|LogFbx: Error' })
$ok = @($ours | Where-Object { $_ -match 'import_pistol: OK' }).Count -gt 0

$ours | ForEach-Object { ($_ -replace '^\[[^\]]*\]\[[^\]]*\]', '').Trim() }
if ($errors.Count -gt 0) {
    Write-Host '---- errors ----'
    $errors | Select-Object -First 60 | ForEach-Object { ($_ -replace '^\[[^\]]*\]\[[^\]]*\]', '').Trim() }
}
Write-Host ("Import: ok={0} errors={1} exit={2} wall={3:N0} s  log: {4}" -f $ok, $errors.Count, $p.ExitCode, $sw.Elapsed.TotalSeconds, $log)
if ($ok -and $errors.Count -eq 0 -and -not $timedOut) { Write-Host 'OK'; exit 0 }
Write-Host 'FAILED'
exit 1
